Palace: Those behind ‘ghost internet’ projects must be held accountable – Presidential Communications Office (https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/palace-those-behind-ghost-internet-projects-must-be-held-accountable/)

News Release
Palace: Those behind ‘ghost internet’ projects must be held accountable
September 25, 2026

Malacañang on Friday said contractors and individuals found responsible for alleged “ghost internet” projects must be held accountable.

At a Palace press briefing, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary and Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said a thorough investigation is needed to identify those who failed to deliver services using public funds.

“Kung gagamit ang mga mapang-abusong businessmen o negosyante na ito at kukulangan ang dapat na ibigay sa ating mga kababayan, hindi sila dapat santuhin. Dapat silang mapanagot,” she added.

Castro stressed that the matter should be investigated immediately, noting that President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. wants to ensure reliable internet connectivity for students and schools.

“Dapat itong tugunan agad, ang pag-iimbestiga dito, dahil ang nais po ng Pangulo, lahat ay dapat konektado. Unang-una niyang concern ay mga mag-aaral. Kailangan na ang mga bata, ang eskuwelahan ay konektado,” she said.

Castro said the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), under Secretary Henry Aguda, should determine what went wrong and identify those who may have abused public funds.

“Dapat din sa pamumuno ni Secretary Aguda ng DICT dapat matumbok, malaman, ma-identify kung sino-sino ang mga ito. Kung saan nagkulang, kung sino ang umaabuso sa pondo ng bayan,” she said.

The Office of the Ombudsman is investigating an alleged “ghost internet” scheme involving DICT projects, including claims involving non-operational or “ghost” internet sites and the delivery of substandard equipment and services. | PND
